capture_method: Native composed game frame / ScreenCapture + triple-buffered AsyncGPUReadback / FFmpeg H.264, 30 fps. Actual real-time playback, no offline motion interpolation.
benchmark_conditions: Windows development standalone, 1280x1000, one player process, three views plus two own-limb overlays, 4x MSAA, shadows, original mesh/texture detail. Editor open with Play Mode stopped. Recording disabled for each separate 90-second benchmark. Other desktop/agent tools remain open; not an isolated laboratory benchmark.

visual_inspection.observation: Both variants show upright guard, readable opponent body and own forearms entering from the bottom edge. Team shoulder ornament remains large at the lower-left of P2 view. Finger silhouette remains an art limitation.
Side-kick chamber and own foot are visible. Guided skirt retains connected pleats rather than the former collapsed cage; lift is still stylized/stiff and does not prove no penetration.
Airborne spinning kick is visible in the arena and both player windows. Waist/interior black seams and local intersections remain visible, especially in the opponent window.

visual_inspection.scope: These are spot checks extracted from the two complete real-time videos, not a quantified naturalness score or a frame-by-frame clothing collision audit.

limits: Edited public CMU motion rehearsal, not live Gemini camera input or two autonomous players.
The native demo replays standard-skeleton combat outcomes; teammate armour has not been fitted to independent hit volumes.
No zero-penetration guarantee. High kick waist, sleeves, fingers and generated mesh seams remain imperfect; skirt shape guides can look stiff.
First-person limbs use a separate projection and view-only IK; this is a screen-game view, not calibrated VR. The large FBX shoulder ornament still appears along the lower-left edge.
Finger closure is a pose prior, not measured finger tracking. Team FBX hat and long ornaments follow existing skin weights; no independent secondary-motion rig was supplied.

Sole-height check is nine static samples, not a continuous slip metric. Performance was measured only on this RTX 4060 Laptop GPU; camera, tracking, network latency and lower-end hardware remain unmeasured.
The two dense VRMs averaged 58 fps with 23.24 ms p95 frame time here; a stable 60 fps target is not yet met for that configuration. The teammate FBX result must not be substituted for it.
